attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: Firm 'cannot' with the antecedent kept: if hyperscalers keep putting 3x+ their AI revenue into capex every year. No deadline was stated.

contract.note: Reading 'pay off' as recovering cost through cumulative net cash returns is a fair, ordinary reading. The contract openly flags the total-capex vs AI-capex mismatch. It rightly requires separate evidence for the antecedent.

evidence.note: Amazon's own disclosure of an AI run rate above $25B. A run rate is not realized annual AI revenue, so it cannot establish the 3x antecedent or any investment recovery.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. The antecedent (capex of 3x+ realized AI revenue every year) is not shown for any hyperscaler; the packet has only Amazon's run-rate figure. There is no cumulative AI cash-return record. With the antecedent unknown and no conclusive event, the claim cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'I believe ... will go unpaid' is an unqualified expectation, not a graded hedge, so it is scored as a forecast. The proposition keeps 'vast majority', the hundreds-of-billions scale and 'indeterminate levels'. No horizon was stated.

contract.note: Weighting by principal for the loan cohort outstanding at publication, and reading 'unpaid' as lasting nonpayment after recoveries, are fair plain readings. Declining to invent a numeric cutoff for 'vast majority' is appropriate.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's own disclosure of convertible notes due 2033, issued after publication. These are notes outside the loan cohort, and the disclosure shows no realized nonpayment.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The packet does not verify the size of the loan stock at publication, and it holds no repayment, default or write-off data for the cohort. The only item is a later note issuance maturing in 2033. Neither the scale clause nor the nonpayment forecast can be settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: The main assertion is a counterfactual argument that the growth needed is 'impossible', with no defined boundary. The unprofitability aside is checkable, but it is secondary. Labeling the whole claim as an observation overstates how testable it is.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no fair binary test for 'impossible' growth without supplying an economic model the speaker never gave. Scoring only the aside would leave out the main claim.

reviews.rationale: The core proposition, that OpenAI and Anthropic would need to grow at an 'impossible' rate even if profitable, sets no feasibility boundary, growth metric or time frame. It is rhetorical and untestable as written. The packet has no evidence items, and none could settle it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: The proposition states both parts faithfully: the labs are the largest cloud customers, and they cannot afford the payments without continuing outside financing.

contract.note: Treating 'near-infinite' as emphasis, reading 'largest' as the leading customers collectively, and using Q2 2026 are fair, ordinary readings. Requiring cash-flow evidence rather than accounting losses alone is reasonable.

evidence.note: Jefferies estimates the labs' combined Q2 share: about 45% of GCP revenue, 25% of Azure and 6% of AWS. These are combined shares, not customer rankings, and the low AWS share leaves 'largest' unsettled there.
Anthropic's H1 net loss was largely driven by financing-related accounting, and the company says it may need more financing. This neither shows it can pay without new funding nor proves it cannot.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows heavy revenue concentration in the labs at GCP and Azure, but no customer-level rankings, and AWS exposure was about 6%. Nothing in the packet is a matched cash-flow, liquidity and payment analysis for both labs. Neither the 'largest' part nor the 'cannot afford' part is settled for Q2 2026.
